summary: @servicetitan/document-title preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes large obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a small React helper for setting document.title, but its package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs` that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is an obfuscated script that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, unpacks it into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it (`execFileSync`) against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~720KB Bun-CJS bundle whose identifiers and string literals are hidden behind a rotated string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shift-rotation with a custom-alphabet numeric-index lookup), so its behavior cannot be inspected without executing it under Bun. A document.title helper does not require a second language runtime or a 700KB opaque module; the shipped code has no observable relationship to the advertised API. The combination of an install-time hook, a dropped alien runtime used to bypass Node-visible code paths, and a large obfuscated bundle executed by that runtime matches the alternate-runtime-dropper supply-chain pattern and executes on any machine that runs `npm install` for this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
